# Decisions: initiative-lifecycle

- 2026-08-05T14:14:41.278Z — chose **Closing an initiative UNBINDS every branch pointing at it (user ruling, 2026-08-05). Reopening happens by binding again, which is a new-session act. The current session is not disrupted: its statusline keeps showing the closed record and its hooks keep routing, because every surface resolves SESSION FIRST and branch binding second.** over (a) Warn but never touch the binding — closing stays a record fact and the branch keeps pointing at finished work, so a fresh session still lands on it and must switch by hand. (b) Infer closure from all-phases-resolved and add no state — cannot tell "finished" from "abandoned at 3/10", cannot express "closed, but 4.1 was never built", and records no when or why. because A binding that outlives the work it points at is how a fresh session ends up oriented on something already finished — the concrete symptom the user hit: a new session's statusline reading `auto-update 11/11`. Unbinding makes the branch honestly say "nothing here" instead. Session-first resolution is what makes unbinding safe rather than destructive: verified that with the branch unbound today, the statusline's record segment vanishes entirely and the PostToolUse hook exits 0 while silently dropping the event, so the rest of the session would go dark. The write path already resolves session-before-branch (context.ts:285) — extending that precedence to the read surfaces makes closing a clean boundary at the SESSION edge rather than a mid-session cliff, and is strictly better behavior even for records that are never closed.
- 2026-08-05T15:07:30.756Z — chose **Reuse the existing log-derived homeInitiative() scan as the cross-process session→initiative mechanism, and share event.ts's resolveBound precedence (branch computed as the PREFERRED candidate, session home wins, branch as fallback) across statusline and hooks** over Persisting the pin to a second store (e.g. .sofar/sessions/<id>) for a single cheap read because Measured on the real 22-initiative, 2.8 MB record: the statusline costs ~55 ms end-to-end today (node startup + fold dominate), and homeInitiative adds 0.07 ms on the hit path (+0.1%, invisible) and 2.9 ms on a full-scan miss (+5%) — and the miss only occurs on the unbound/re-homed path that closing creates. The cost that worried this task is not there. A persisted pin would be a second store that can desync from the truth log, which record-integrity D1 already ruled against, and would need stale-pin cleanup the scan does not. Decisive: the mechanism is already proven in production — hooks route correctly on a fully unbound branch today (measured against published 0.18.0), so this reuses a shipped, tested path instead of introducing a parallel one.
- 2026-08-05T15:08:23.893Z — chose **When neither a session pin nor a branch binding resolves, hooks keep dropping the event silently (exit 0, never lazily bind) — but the CONDITION becomes observable once per session at the two orienting surfaces that already run: SessionStart injects an unbound notice naming `sofar new` / `sofar switch` (4.1), and the statusline renders an explicit unbound marker instead of merely omitting the record segment (3.2)** over (i) lazily binding the branch at hook time; (ii) warning on stderr per dropped event; (iii) recording drops to a sidecar file outside the event log because The drop is per-event but the condition is per-session — "this session is registered nowhere and the branch is unbound" is ONE fact, so it belongs once where the agent reads, not N times where nothing does. (i) is disqualified twice over: it recreates the misrouting record-integrity 1.2/D1 fixed, and it would let a hook silently undo a close — 1.1 measured that no engine path re-creates a binding today (only new/switch write bindings.json), and that property is what makes close-unbinds safe. (ii) fires on every tool use, so the noise scales with work, and BD22 says never break the session. (iii) is a second store outside the truth log, which record-integrity D1 rules against — the same reason 1.2 rejected a persisted pin. Measured today: on an unbound branch with an unregistered session, SessionStart injects 0 bytes and the statusline renders `repo · main` — both silently indistinguishable from a healthy repo, which is the actual defect.
- 2026-08-05T15:12:39.810Z — chose **`sofar switch <closed-slug>` reopens the initiative — it appends initiative_status_changed{status:'active'} and binds the branch, with no flag required — but never silently: the reopen is announced in the confirmation and recorded as an event, exactly as the close was** over Refusing a closed slug outright, or requiring an explicit --reopen flag because The user's rule is that working on it again is what revives it, and `switch` IS that act — it means "this branch works on this now", which a closed record cannot honour while staying closed. Refusing makes closing a dead end, which the rule forbids. A --reopen flag only adds a step to a decision the user already expressed by typing switch; the flag would be discoverable solely by hitting the refusal it exists to bypass. Reading a closed record needs no binding (`sofar status <slug>` already does that), so switch is never the accidental path. The event keeps the revival auditable — the log shows closed-then-reopened rather than an unexplained return to active, which is what append-only history is for.
